title: Adolescent exposure to organophosphate insecticide malathion induces spermatogenesis dysfunction in mice by activating the HIF-1/MAPK/PI3K pathway.
authors: Xiao, Shouchun; Cui, Jingna; Cao, Yue; Zhang, Yaru; Yang, Jiaxing; Zheng, Li; Zhao, Fanrong; Liu, Xueke; Zhou, Zhiqiang; Liu, Donghui; Wang, Peng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究马拉硫磷暴露通过HIF-1/MAPK/PI3K通路致小鼠精子发生障碍，分子对接仅验证小分子与蛋白结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Chemical-caused reproductive dysfunction has emerged as a global public health concern. This study investigated the adverse effects of the organophosphorus pesticide malathion on reproductive function in adolescent male mice at environmentally relevant concentrations. The results indicated that eight-week malathion exposure reduced testis weight, caused sex and thyroid hormone disorders, and induced testicular spermatogenic epithelium damage and oxidative stress. Testicular RNA sequencing indicated that malathion significantly affected testicular energy metabolism, hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1) signaling, and steroid hormone biosynthesis pathways. Malathion significantly increased the gene and protein expression of HIF-1alpha by upregulating key genes in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway (Map2k2, Mapk3, and Eif4e2) and the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway (Pik3r2 and Akt1). Furthermore, malathion downregulated HIF-1alpha degradation-regulating genes while upregulating anaerobic metabolism and inflammation-related genes, thereby inhibiting normoxia and promoting hypoxia processes. Testicular hypoxia subsequently induced steroid hormone biosynthesis disorders and spermatogenesis dysfunction. Molecular docking verified that malathion interfered with HIF-1alpha and steroid hormone synthases (CYP11A1, CYP17A1 and CYP19A1) by forming hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions with these proteins. This study presents the first evidence that malathion triggers spermatogenesis dysfunction in mice through activating the HIF-1/MAPK/PI3K pathway, providing a comprehensive understanding of the reproductive toxicity risks associated with organophosphorus pesticides.
abstract_zh: 化学品引起的生殖功能障碍已成为全球公共卫生关注的问题。本研究探讨了有机磷农药马拉硫磷在环境相关浓度下对青春期雄性小鼠生殖功能的不良影响。结果表明，八周马拉硫磷暴露降低了睾丸重量，导致性激素和甲状腺激素紊乱，并诱发睾丸生精上皮损伤和氧化应激。睾丸RNA测序显示，马拉硫磷显著影响睾丸能量代谢、缺氧诱导因子1（HIF-1）信号通路和类固醇激素生物合成途径。马拉硫磷通过上调丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）通路关键基因（Map2k2、Mapk3和Eif4e2）和磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（PI3K）通路关键基因（Pik3r2和Akt1），显著增加HIF-1α的基因和蛋白表达。此外，马拉硫磷下调了调控HIF-1α降解的基因，同时上调了无氧代谢和炎症相关基因，从而抑制常氧并促进缺氧过程。睾丸缺氧随后诱导类固醇激素生物合成紊乱和生精功能障碍。分子对接验证了马拉硫磷通过形成氢键和疏水相互作用与HIF-1α及类固醇激素合成酶（CYP11A1、CYP17A1和CYP19A1）发生干扰。本研究首次提供证据表明，马拉硫磷通过激活HIF-1/MAPK/PI3K通路触发小鼠生精功能障碍，为全面理解有机磷农药相关的生殖毒性风险提供了依据。
